initial.name: run_code
initial.description: Execute a TypeScript program against the available tools. Takes two required arguments: `description`, a short summary of what the program does, and `code`, the program to execute. Call tools as `await tools.name(args)` per the declarations in the system prompt. Curate the program output. Image-bearing subtool results are attached after the run. The program contains TypeScript REPL statements; only erasable syntax is accepted, with no enum or namespaces. Type annotations are advisory. Top-level declarations and await are supported; top-level return is not supported. Emit output with console.log(...) or a final lossless JSON expression. Only printed values and that final expression become program output. Variables, functions, and imported modules remain in memory for this Agent across calls. Use await import(...) for modules. This environment has full host access without a file sandbox; process.env starts empty. Restart, Agent disposal, cancellation, timeout, output overflow, or process failure clears the environment. If a variable is undefined, recreate it and reacquire its resources. State is not restored from the conversation, and failed evaluations can leave earlier mutations in memory. Redeclaring an existing let, const, or class name fails; assign to a mutable binding or use a new name. Await all tool calls; background callbacks cannot call tools after their evaluation ends. Await child-process completion before ending an evaluation; raw subprocess output belongs to whichever evaluation is active when it arrives. Each program starts in the Session's current directory. Running programs keep their initial directory.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this program does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Provide `description` before `code` in the arguments. Examples: "Count TODO markers across packages"; "Read failing test and its fixture"; "Rename config key in every cordis.yml".

code.description: The TypeScript program to execute, following this tool's execution instructions.

timeoutMs.description: Positive elapsed-time budget in milliseconds, including nested tool and approval waits. Default 120000; capped at 600000. Zero does not disable the deadline.
